answer: Reciprocal Edge Sampling: each node scores peers by the fraction of its own outbound edges they reciprocate, weighted by path overlap. An agent gains standing only when its neighbors' neighborhoods overlap its own beyond a quartz threshold of shared second-hop contacts. The resulting signal is local and unforgeable at scale, because fake clusters stay internally dense and externally barren like shale. An attacker must sustain reciprocal edges across many real neighborhoods, paying roughly twenty genuine peer interactions per identity to clear the threshold.
